future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: I have a toy car.
Childhood was hard.
You will be asking for forgiveness.

examples.trans: How is it in Hungary?
I grew up in a communal flat.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to come back, to return', paired with 'возвращаться'.

examples.trans: I'll be back soon.
He came back home.

examples.text: Так, не шумим. Я скоро вернусь.
examples.trans: Right, no noise. I'll be back soon.

meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'сход'). Common masculine noun meaning 'with the rising / sunrise' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Но с восходом солнца появляются новые причины жить дальше.
examples.trans: But with the sunrise come new reasons to keep living.

examples.text: На кухне ресторана всегда есть восход.
examples.trans: In the restaurant kitchen there is always with the rising.

meanings.note: Qualitative adjective. Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'сокий'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('high, tall').

examples.trans: He has a high temperature.
This is a tall building.
He developed a high temperature.

meanings.note: In a list or a story. Core Russian adv meaning 'next; further' in everyday speech.
In a list or a story. Core Russian adv meaning 'next; further' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: All right. Next.
What's next?

examples.text: А дальше? Я очень волнуюсь, я к этому не приспособлена.
examples.trans: And then what? I'm very nervous, I'm not cut out for this.

meanings.note: Colloquial. Common masculine noun meaning 'grandfather' in everyday Russian.
Colloquial. Common masculine noun meaning 'grandfather' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: У меня дед три года партизанил!
examples.trans: My grandfather was a partisan for three years!
My grandfather lives in the country.

examples.text: Я никого пытать не буду, ясно? У меня дед три года партизанил!
examples.trans: I'm not going to torture anyone, got it? My grandfather was a partisan for three years!

meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'until, before; up to' in everyday speech.
Core Russian prep meaning 'until, before; up to' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Goodbye!
See you tomorrow!
See you tonight!

related.gloss: to reach, walk as far as

meanings.note: + infinitive; agrees with the subject: должна (f)
Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'лжен'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('must, should; owe').

examples.trans: I have to work.
Greed should be moderate.

examples.text: Жадность, Паша, должна быть умеренная. Комнатной температуры.
examples.trans: Greed, Pasha, should be moderate. Room temperature.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'friend' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is Vanya, my childhood friend.
He's my friend.

examples.text: Это Паша, мой заместитель. Это Ваня, друг моего детства.
examples.trans: This is Pasha, my deputy. This is Vanya, my childhood friend.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'spirit / ghost' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Это дух умершего человека, который вернулся мстить!
examples.trans: It is the spirit of a dead person who came back to take revenge!

examples.text: На кухне ресторана всегда есть дух.
examples.trans: In the restaurant kitchen there is always spirit.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to live'.

examples.trans: I live in a communal flat.
I want to live normally.

examples.text: Я хочу нормально жить! Я хочу биде, понимаешь?
examples.trans: I want to live like a normal person! I want a bidet, do you understand?

meanings.note: Спасибо за + accusative. Core Russian prep meaning 'for; behind' in everyday speech.
+ instrumental. Core Russian prep meaning 'for; behind' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Thank you for your trust!
Thanks for the present.
What for?

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'втра').

examples.trans: We'll arrange something for tomorrow.
See you tomorrow!

examples.text: Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.

meanings.note: Prefix 'из-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'ысканный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('exquisite / refined').

examples.text: Что-то изысканное, как сама прекрасная Франция!
examples.trans: Something exquisite, like beautiful France itself!

examples.text: Зайка, вкус у тебя действительно очень изысканный!
examples.trans: Sweetheart, your taste is truly very exquisite!

meanings.note: Искусство войны = The Art of War. Prefix 'ис-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'кусство'). Common neuter noun meaning 'art, skill' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Read The Art of War, by Sun Tzu!
She loves modern art very much.
This is a real culinary work of art!

meanings.note: Question word. Core Russian adv meaning 'how; as' in everyday speech.
Как вы знаете = as you know. Core Russian adv meaning 'how; as' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: How was it in Hungary?

Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'Kirill' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Grandpa Kirill is having a flare-up again.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to copy'.

examples.trans: You cannot simply copy other people's dishes.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и копировать вовремя.

examples.trans: And the kitchen is over there.

examples.text: Проходите, пожалуйста! Как видите, большой коридор, а там кухня.
examples.trans: Come on in, please! As you can see, a big hall, and the kitchen is over there.

meanings.note: Short for может быть. Core Russian part meaning 'maybe, perhaps' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.

Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'стоящий'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('real, genuine').

examples.trans: Nobody is going to give orders in my kitchen!

examples.text: Не говори об этом никому, ладно?

meanings.note: Stronger contrast than 'а'. Core Russian conj meaning 'but' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('new').

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('lonely, alone').

examples.text: Костя, быстро попробуй мой новый паштет.
examples.trans: Kostya, quickly taste my new pâté.

повторить.gloss: to repeat, to go over again

meanings.en: to repeat, to say or do again
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'вторить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to repeat, to go over again', paired with 'повторять'.

examples.trans: Right, let's go over it again.
Repeat that, please.
So, repeat that clearly once more.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'гружать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'plunges / immerses'.

examples.text: Расставание погружает тебя в холодную, одинокую ночь.
examples.trans: A breakup plunges you into a cold, lonely night.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и погружать вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and plunges on time.

meanings.note: Подожди! = wait!. Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'ождать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to wait (a while)', paired with 'ждать'.

examples.trans: Wait, I'll be right there.
Wait a minute.

examples.text: Подожди, Нин, ты не поняла. Это же стыдно!
examples.trans: Wait, Nina, you don't get it. It's shameful!

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'лтергейст'). Common masculine noun meaning 'poltergeist' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Could it be a real poltergeist?

examples.text: Украл мясо и сразу свалил на полтергейст!
examples.trans: You steal meat and immediately blame it on the poltergeist!
Of course, the evil poltergeist did it!

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'являться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to appear'.

examples.text: Нам не надо появляться на работе вместе.
examples.trans: We do not need to appear at work together.

examples.text: Нам лучше пока не появляться на работе вместе по утрам.
examples.trans: We had better not show up at work together in the mornings for now.

examples.text: В меню каждую весну появляются новые лёгкие салаты.
examples.trans: New light salads appear on the menu every spring.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('beautiful, wonderful').

examples.trans: A beautiful town!
A wonderful idea.

examples.text: Посмотри, какой у нас город прекрасный. Озёра, луга.
examples.trans: Look what a beautiful town we have. Lakes, meadows.

придумать.gloss: to think up, to come up with

meanings.en: to think up, to invent, to come up with
meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'думать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to think up, to come up with', paired with 'придумывать'.

examples.trans: You came up with this yourself!
I'll think up a plan.

examples.text: Как нет? Ты же сам это всё придумал!
examples.trans: What do you mean, no time? You came up with all this yourself!

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'чина'). Common feminine noun meaning 'reason, cause' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Нет причин держать вас под арестом.
examples.trans: There is no reason to keep you under arrest.
What is the reason?

examples.text: Нет причин держать вас под арестом. Сегодня вы выйдете отсюда.
examples.trans: There is no reason to keep you under arrest. Today you will walk out of here.

meanings.en: to happen, take place, go on
meanings.note: Что происходит? = What is going on?

examples.trans: What is going on? I don't understand.
What is happening here?

examples.text: Мы не знаем, что с нашей дочерью происходит!
examples.trans: We don't know what is happening with our daughter!

meanings.note: 'это просто' = it's easy. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
Это просто = it's easy. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I'm just tired.
It's easy.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: Простые люди = ordinary people. Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'стой'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('simple; ordinary').

Простые люди = ordinary people. Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'стой'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('simple; ordinary').

examples.trans: That's a simple question.
He's an ordinary man.

meanings.note: Prefix 'рас-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'ставание'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'breakup / parting' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: You two had a hard breakup.

examples.text: На кухне ресторана всегда есть расставание.
examples.trans: In the restaurant kitchen there is always breakup.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'recipe', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Шеф хранит свой тайный рецепт супа.
examples.trans: The chef keeps his secret soup recipe.

examples.text: Да? Это мой старый фирменный рецепт.
examples.trans: Really? This is my old signature recipe.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share with everyone.

meanings.note: Сам, сама, само, сами. Core Russian pron meaning 'oneself (myself, yourself...)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

meanings.note: colloquial: нет света = the power is off
colloquial: нет света = the power is off

examples.trans: Say a firework hit the power station. Three districts without electricity.

meanings.note: refers back to the subject: 'он держит своё слово' = he keeps his word

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'олнце'). Common neuter noun meaning 'sun' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Мы идём вверх, прямо к солнцу.
examples.trans: We are walking up, straight to the sun.

meanings.en: to go on, be happening (usually of chaos or strange events)
meanings.note: 3rd person only. Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to go on, to happen'.

examples.trans: So much is going on in the country!

meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I have a toy car.
He's at our place.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.
examples.trans: Hi! Look what I've got.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'мерший'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('deceased / dead').

examples.text: Это дух умершего человека, который вернулся мстить!
examples.trans: It is the spirit of a dead person who came back to take revenge!

examples.text: Шеф говорит, что это очень умерший выбор.
examples.trans: The chef says that this is a very deceased choice.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'никальный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('unique').

examples.trans: You get unique flavours.

examples.text: И огурцы тоже можно, можно всё, что хотите! Получаются уникальные вкусы.
examples.trans: And cucumbers are fine too, anything you want! You get unique flavours.

examples.text: Главное сохранить этот уникальный древний монастырь.
examples.trans: The main thing is to preserve this unique ancient monastery.

meanings.note: Qualitative or relational adjective formed with the productive '-н-' suffix, meaning 'signature' and agreeing in gender, number, and case.

examples.trans: This is signature, specialty.

examples.text: Я могу приготовить своё фирменное блюдо.
examples.trans: I can prepare my signature dish.
The chef prepared his signature dish.

meanings.note: Low temperature. Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('cold, chilly; distant').
Emotion. Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('cold, chilly; distant').

examples.trans: Cold vodka.
You are a good woman. Cold.
Cold.

meanings.note: the plural is a different word: люди, людям, о людях
Plural люди, a different word. Common masculine noun meaning 'person; (pl) people' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: He is a good person.
There are a lot of people here.
I know the problems of ordinary people.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'devilry / spooky nonsense' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Что это за чертовщина тут творится?
examples.trans: What kind of devilry is going on in here?

examples.text: Шеф, тут такая чертовщина, я ночью не останусь!
examples.trans: Chef, with such spooky nonsense here, I am not staying at night!

examples.text: Дима, действительно, на кухне творится какая-то чертовщина!
examples.trans: Dima, really, some kind of devilry is going on in the kitchen!

meanings.note: Question word. Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.
Conjunction. Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.
Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: What's this?
Look what I've got.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.
examples.trans: Hi! Look what I've got.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'something; somehow', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Did something happen?
Has something happened?
Somehow I'm tired.

meanings.note: neuter чужое as a noun = other people's things
Чужой человек = a stranger. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('someone else's, foreign').

examples.text: Вы так и берёте чужое без спроса?
examples.trans: So you just take other people's things without asking?
That's someone else's bag.

examples.text: Вы так и берёте чужое без спроса, да?
examples.trans: So you just take other people's things without asking, yes?

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Linking word: главное — это народ. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: That's mine.
And this is for you.
And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'I' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I'm doing my homework.
I grew up here.
Chef, I didn't take it.
